scene-home.label: The Digital Agency
scene-home.title: The purpose is not fewer people. It is more human work.
paragraphs: The Digital Agency is an enterprise where intelligence becomes part of the workforce: present in the flow of work, able to accept outcomes, and governed with the same seriousness as any other operating capability.

Its purpose is not to automate humanity out of the organization. It is to absorb coordination, repetition, and administrative friction so people can spend more attention on judgment, creativity, relationships, and responsibility.
scene-home.takeaway: Use digital labor to expand human agency, not diminish it.

scene-event.label: Before we begin
scene-event.title: A moment to arrive.
paragraphs: This opening image is an invitation to step out of the daily rush and into a longer view of work. The next twenty minutes are not about another feature release. They are about a change in the shape of the enterprise.
As you move forward, notice how the story travels from tools, to agency, to operating models, and finally to the leadership choices that determine whether this transition creates value.
scene-event.takeaway: The technology is moving quickly. The purpose of this experience is to create enough space to decide where we want it to take us.

scene-audience-guide.label: Join the conversation
scene-audience-guide.title: This experience has a live pulse.
paragraphs: The QR code opens a lightweight reaction page on your phone. Tap whenever an idea resonates, surprises you, raises a question, or needs clarification.
Your reaction rises onto the shared screen in real time. There is no form to complete and no need to wait for a formal Q&A moment; the room can respond while the story is unfolding.
scene-audience-guide.takeaway: Scan once, keep the page open, and react as often as you like throughout the experience.

scene-one.label: The agentic enterprise
scene-one.title: AI is becoming a participant in work.
paragraphs: The first wave of enterprise AI sat beside us. It helped draft, summarize, search, and prepare. That was a meaningful shift, but it kept the human at the center of every action.
The next wave moves from assistance to participation. Digital colleagues will carry context, accept delegated outcomes, coordinate with people and systems, and return with work completed.
scene-one.takeaway: The question is no longer only how people use AI. It is how people and AI share work, accountability, and outcomes.

sandvik.label: Adoption was the spark
sandvik.title: Prompting changed tasks. Agency changes the system.
paragraphs: Prompting taught millions of people that natural language could become a new interface to knowledge work. It reduced friction and made intelligence feel immediately accessible.

But prompting is still a request-and-response model. Agency begins when AI can hold a goal, decide what to do next, use tools, coordinate steps, and operate within boundaries without waiting for every instruction.
sandvik.takeaway: Prompt adoption was the beginning. The strategic work starts when delegation becomes possible.

scene-speaker.label: Your guide
scene-speaker.title: Why I care about this transition.
paragraphs: My work sits between technology architecture and organizational reality. I see what becomes possible when new capabilities arrive, and I also see the distance between a compelling demonstration and dependable enterprise value.
This story is designed for leaders making choices about that distance: what to scale, what to govern, what to redesign, and what must remain deeply human.
scene-speaker.takeaway: Treat this as a strategic conversation, not a product pitch.

scene-three.label: A compressed history
scene-three.title: Intelligence is moving closer to action.
paragraphs: For decades, each technology era changed how quickly information could move: mainframes centralized it, personal computers distributed it, the internet connected it, mobile made it ambient, and cloud made it elastic.

The recent acceleration is different. Chatbots made intelligence conversational. Copilots placed it inside the flow of work. Agents connect intelligence to tools and actions. Digital colleagues add continuity, role, and collaboration.
scene-three.takeaway: The defining movement is not simply more intelligence. It is less distance between understanding, deciding, and acting.

scene-shifts.label: Shift 1 · The operating model
scene-shifts.title: The first shift is from conversation to digital labor.
paragraphs: Conversation lets us ask. Collaboration lets us create together. Delegation lets us assign an outcome instead of describing every step. Digital labor extends that delegation into repeatable, autonomous work.

These are not interchangeable maturity labels. Every step asks for stronger context, clearer authority, better controls, and a more explicit understanding of who owns the result. That changing operating model also changes where people sit in the work.
scene-shifts.takeaway: Capability rises with autonomy, but so does the need for operating discipline.

scene-human-loop.label: Shift 2 · The human role
scene-human-loop.title: As agency grows, people move from execution to oversight.
paragraphs: Human in the loop means a person remains part of each task and decision. Human on the loop shifts the person into supervision: AI performs more of the work while people monitor, guide, and intervene when needed.

Human off the loop describes bounded autonomy. Agents coordinate tools, memory, and specialist roles without continuous attention, while people retain authority over goals, policies, exceptions, and accountability. Once that autonomy persists, an agent begins to look less like a feature and more like an organizational role.
scene-human-loop.takeaway: Less human involvement in execution requires more deliberate boundaries, observability, and escalation design.

scene-agent-evolution.label: Shift 3 · Role-based autonomy
scene-agent-evolution.title: Agents are evolving from a capability into a role.
paragraphs: Interactive agents perform a defined task when asked. Autonomous agents can plan toward an outcome, coordinate tools, and collaborate with other agents across a more complex workflow.

Role-based autonomy adds persistent identity, organizational context, access, communication channels, and a place in enterprise systems. The shift is from invoking a tool to working with a governed participant, which raises a practical question: where does that participant sit in the organization?
scene-agent-evolution.takeaway: The defining change is not greater autonomy alone; it is durable identity, access, responsibility, and accountability.

scene-org.label: The new organizational chart
scene-org.title: Role-based agents turn the org chart into a mixed workforce.
paragraphs: This is not a chart of humans being replaced. It is a chart of work being redistributed. People continue to set direction, exercise judgment, build trust, and carry accountability while specialized AI roles research, analyze, track, and prepare.

The Agency makes this concrete: signals become analysis, commitments become visible, drafts arrive ready for judgment, and only the decisions that genuinely need a leader are escalated. A mixed workforce like this cannot run on isolated tools; it needs a shared enterprise architecture.
scene-org.takeaway: The future org chart describes responsibilities and decision rights, not only reporting lines.

scene-multimodal.label: Multimodal intelligence
scene-multimodal.title: Orchestrated AI can understand more of the real work environment.
paragraphs: Routing and collaboration become more useful when AI can understand the work itself. Work rarely arrives as clean text; it lives in meetings, images, screens, documents, video, data, and the relationships between them.

When multimodal understanding is connected to reasoning and tools, AI can inspect a situation, identify what matters, prepare a response, and act. That expanded ability is exactly why the next part of the story must be governance.
scene-multimodal.takeaway: Multimodality expands what AI can understand; governance determines what it should be allowed to do.

scene-four.label: Multi-model enterprise
scene-four.title: There will not be one permanent winner.
paragraphs: A platform designed to outlive every model must treat model diversity as a feature. Different work demands different intelligence: a frontier model for complex reasoning, a small model for speed and cost, an open model for control, or a specialist model for a narrow domain.
The moving orbits represent a portfolio that will keep changing. The durable enterprise capability is the route at the center: selecting models by task, risk, performance, policy, and economics.
scene-four.takeaway: Competitive advantage shifts from choosing a model to governing a portfolio of intelligence.

scene-orchestration.label: From selection to orchestration
scene-orchestration.title: Model choice becomes a system decision.
paragraphs: Once the enterprise manages a portfolio, people cannot choose every model for every task. Platform routing uses context, policy, capability, latency, and cost to determine the best fit automatically.
Beyond routing, specialized models and agents can collaborate: one investigates, another verifies, another acts, and an evaluation layer checks the result.
scene-orchestration.takeaway: The strategic asset is not a single model. It is the orchestration, evaluation, and control layer around them.

scene-ai-architecture.label: Intelligence + Trust
scene-ai-architecture.title: A mixed workforce needs connected intelligence and trust.
paragraphs: The architecture brings Microsoft 365 Copilot, Cowork, agents, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, Fabric, Foundry, Azure, and Agent 365 into one governed system rather than a collection of disconnected tools.
Microsoft IQ sits at the center, connecting Work IQ, Foundry IQ, and Fabric IQ so experiences can share organizational context while security forms the boundary around every layer.
scene-ai-architecture.takeaway: The differentiator is not only intelligence. It is intelligence connected to enterprise context and bounded by trust.

scene-ms-approach.label: The Microsoft AI Approach
scene-ms-approach.title: One experience, different levels of agency.
paragraphs: With the architecture in place, the Microsoft AI approach brings several working modes into one Copilot experience. Chat assists with secure enterprise conversation. Cowork and Code move toward delegated, multi-step execution. Autopilots represent digital teams that can sustain work over time.

The important progression is not a collection of separate destinations. It is a continuum of agency: from helping a person complete a task, to accepting outcomes, using multiple tools, and coordinating work with less supervision.
scene-ms-approach.takeaway: One Copilot can meet people where they are today while creating a path toward delegated and autonomous work.

scene-copilot-strategy.label: Platform strategy
scene-copilot-strategy.title: The platform must outlive every model.
paragraphs: Turning that continuum of agency into a durable enterprise capability requires a platform that can evolve. Microsoft's strategy begins with a multi-model foundation so enterprises can adopt the best intelligence as the market changes without rebuilding.
That flexibility sits on a cloud-native, enterprise-grade foundation grounded in organizational context through WorkIQ, integrated into the flow of work, and protected by security and governance.
scene-copilot-strategy.takeaway: The durable advantage is not betting on one model. It is building a platform that can absorb the next one.

scene-governance.label: Governance as capability
scene-governance.title: Govern what AI sees, does, decides, and uses.
paragraphs: The preceding capabilities increase what AI can perceive and do. Governance begins with data: what an agent can see and how context is protected. It extends to actions and decisions across Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, Fabric, Foundry, and Azure.
Microsoft IQ connects OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta at the intelligence center, while Agent 365 forms the outer management layer across the complete agent estate.
scene-governance.takeaway: Good governance is not a brake on scale. It is the mechanism that makes confident scale possible.

scene-questions.label: Leadership discussion
scene-questions.title: The agentic era begins with choices.
paragraphs: The five questions on screen turn an abstract future into an operating agenda. They ask where delegation creates value, where human authority must remain, and how intelligence should be selected, funded, and managed.
The final question makes the change visible: if digital colleagues become part of the workforce, what does the organizational chart look like, and who is accountable for the work they perform?
scene-questions.takeaway: Do not start with how many agents to deploy. Start with the work, decisions, controls, economics, and accountabilities you want to redesign.

scene-agent-challenge.label: A question for the room
scene-agent-challenge.title: What would slow your organization first?
paragraphs: Imagine that access to AI agents is no longer scarce. Every employee can delegate research, analysis, coordination, and execution to one or more agents.
The constraint then moves away from access. It becomes the organizational capability that is least ready: governance, skills, trust, operating model, or budget.
scene-agent-challenge.takeaway: Choose the first constraint you would need to remove, not the one that is easiest to discuss.

scene-thanks.label: A closing thought
scene-thanks.title: The future of work is a design choice.
paragraphs: The shift from copilots to digital colleagues will not arrive as one launch or one decision. It will emerge through hundreds of choices about work, authority, architecture, and trust.
My hope is that this experience gives you a clearer language for those choices and a reason to begin the conversation before technology makes the default decisions for you.
scene-thanks.takeaway: Thank you for spending this time with the ideas. Keep the conversation going.
